title: Saved-copy shift search with streamed exact arithmetic

claims.statement: For every integer N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, let n = ceil(log2 N), L = 2^n, and k = n+24. The streamed saved-copy shift-search algorithm of proof.md acquires exactly k independent ideal DCP copies once; for n >= 2 it performs r = isqrt(9L) // 4 iterations of its implemented candidate-controlled all-pass reflection and diffusion; for n = 1 (N = 2) it tests t = 0 on all k copies and outputs 0 if all pass and 1 otherwise. The total sequential work in the challenge model is T(N,s) = O(2^(n/2) n^2 log2 n) for n >= 2. A bound valid for all n >= 1 is C 2^(n/2) n^2 max{1,log2 n}, with an absolute C; the n=1 branch has constant work. The eventually positive uniform time envelope B_T(n) = 2^(n/2) n^2 log2 n has exact growth index 1. Work includes initialization, source acquisition, all gates, exact gate decomposition, uniform streamed circuit generation, bit operations, addressing, preprocessing, measurements and output. All constants are absolute and independent of N, s and outcomes. This is a worst-case bound on every execution branch, jointly with the other three resource bounds, the epsilon(n)=0 error model below, and unconditional recovery of the entire s with probability at least 25573/36864 > 2/3.

The total number of source copies is exactly Q(N,s) = n+24 on every execution branch, hence O(n), with uniform envelope B_samples(n) = n and exact growth index 0. All acquired copies and final discards are counted; there are no additional samples for unsuccessful measurements or restarts. All constants are absolute and independent of N, s and outcomes. This is a worst-case bound on every execution branch, jointly with the other three resource bounds, the epsilon(n)=0 error model below, and unconditional recovery of the entire s with probability at least 25573/36864 > 2/3.

For every integer N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, let n = ceil(log2 N), L = 2^n, and k = n+24. The streamed saved-copy shift-search algorithm of proof.md acquires exactly k independent ideal DCP copies once; for n >= 2 it performs r = isqrt(9L) // 4 iterations of its implemented candidate-controlled all-pass reflection and diffusion; for n = 1 (N = 2) it tests t = 0 on all k copies and outputs 0 if all pass and 1 otherwise. The proved fractional error tolerance is epsilon(n)=0 for every N >= 2 and every s. Among Q=n+24 acquired copies, floor(epsilon(n) Q)=0 may be malformed. The delivered joint state must be rho_s^{tensor k}; every clean copy at delivery is independent of the other copies and the algorithm workspace, and the source has no subsequent access to delivered copies. Correlations created subsequently by the algorithm are unrestricted. Under this promise the same algorithm recovers the entire s with unconditional probability at least 25573/36864 > 2/3 jointly with all four stated worst-case resource bounds. No success is promised for malformed copies, and no positive tolerance or impossibility of greater tolerance is asserted.

structured.error_model: Malformed fraction among acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
